validation.independence: RGB matrices derived from primaries and D65 through XYZ. validation.iterative_oracle_change: The old copied iteration hid its own stopping error. Against geometric boundaries, the unchanged P3 f64 Ostrowski iteration reaches 1.2753e-8 linear error under its existing 1e-9 chroma stopping rule; the new geometric mapping limit is 2e-8. Raw-chroma limits are unchanged.
validation.cli: All targets in both timing modes pass; validate-only emits no timing tables. All targets have policy-aware f64 cross-method checks. NaN/infinite outputs and individual metrics are explicitly rejected.

review_resolution.1: Cached and uncached JavaScript upper roots now include zero as the lower bound, with a shared conditioned polynomial solver and both-mode near-white regressions.
review_resolution.2: Replaced the arbitrary tiny-root ratio cutoff with a derivative bound. Also deflate accurately recovered negative roots so they cannot round positive. Native f32 uses its existing stationary-interval candidate validation instead of duplicating the f64 local solve or preliminary Newton polish.
review_resolution.3: Geometric outward intersections replace the unreliable blue-fold second iteration. All channels must be feasible within arithmetic roundoff. Independent tests no longer repeat that iteration.
review_resolution.4: Retained linear RGB comparisons for near-zero gamma behavior and added separate perceptual limits. Encoded maxima remain reported. Rec.2020 encoded error has the finite global bound linear_error^(1/2.4), but it is deliberately not the only accuracy gate.
review_resolution.5: Non-finite outputs were already rejected before aggregation. Added explicit finite-metric checks and injected-regression tests, including the legacy cross-method comparator.
review_resolution.6: Fold windows are shared binary32 endpoints, widened exactly in f64, with endpoint-neighbor tests.
review_resolution.7: Added policy-aware cross-method checks to every target CLI run.
review_resolution.8: Raytrace non-positive chroma uses the canonical achromatic conversion in both modes.
review_resolution.9: Zero-root handling checks outward departure; inward contacts factor out the zero root. A strictly outside neutral returns zero boundary chroma.
review_resolution.10: Only poorly conditioned derivatives require the extra Newton residual evaluation. Necessary-condition rejection avoids division on clear failures; f32 does not repeat its existing root validation. Timings report the full change, not an isolated claimed speedup.
review_resolution.12: Generic clipped conversion delegates to Clip; the P3 LMS-slope wrapper delegates to the shared generic kernel.
review_resolution.13: Cached and uncached solvers share one scalar candidate implementation in Rust and JavaScript.

limitations: Sampled numerical checks on Linux/glibc, not full-domain or cross-platform proofs.

Near fold tangencies and corners, native rounding can change whether an outer island exists; alternate-branch allowances are restricted to independently enumerated feasible intersections near such contacts.
Raytrace has looser native-f32 numerical limits than the boundary solvers; its error maxima and limits are reported separately.
Cached cubic retains its 0.1-degree hue policy and small incumbent Cardano approximation error.
Near-black iterative stopping is assessed through final RGB rather than uniformly tight raw chroma.
No JavaScript timing or multi-gamut performance claim is made.
